fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address markers at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Mark the driveway entrance width clearly so arriving apparatus operators can judge clearance before committing to the approach.
• Post the property address at both the road entrance and again near the main residence, since the length of the driveway may delay responders in confirming they have reached the correct structure.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so arriving and staging apparatus can complete the loop without blocking each other.
• Designate and communicate a specific staging area within the circular driveway for command and support vehicles that will not obstruct the primary apparatus path.
• Identify and mark any secondary access point to the rear of the property so responders are not limited to a single approach during an active incident.
• Post a simple site map near the main entry showing the location of the detached structure, storage area, and any rear access limitations so responders arriving at the front door can orient quickly.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings on foot without obstruction.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible address or unit identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence when communicating over radio.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim any shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to increase open space between tree canopies and the building.
• Cut grass surrounding the structure short, particularly during dry periods.
• Remove dead or dry grass and plant material from areas immediately around the structure.
• Keep low-hanging branches on large trees near the structure trimmed up from the ground.
• Maintain the open green space areas by keeping grass mowed and removing any accumulating dead plant material.
• Thin shrubs scattered across the property to reduce the number of connected plants that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation to allow vehicles to pass freely.
